_about: What a due process hearing officer can generally order, in the words the complaint prints under IV. Proposed resolution. The person drafting chooses; `detail` is their own quantity or specification (never suggested by the skill). Two remedies a hearing officer generally cannot grant are listed as `outsideAuthority` and are not offered — they may be kept only if the person drafting insists, and the report says so. `other` prints exactly what was typed and nothing else. `counselOnly` marks a remedy that exists only on a represented filing: fees are awarded by a court to a prevailing parent under 20 U.S.C. § 1415(i)(3)(B), not by the hearing officer, so the complaint reserves the right rather than asking the officer for them, and a self-represented parent cannot recover them.
